institutions.fact: Political parties select presidential nominees through a nomination process; the Electoral College chooses the president. Holding a national party committee chair is not itself a presidential nomination.
institutions.gameplay_assumption: A separately reviewed presidential contender role is required for a new named national executive. The generic government event does not implement a complete presidential nomination or Electoral College simulation.

institutions.fact: Constitution articles 6 and 7 separate the directly elected President of the Republic from party leadership; article 8 gives the President appointment of the Prime Minister.
institutions.gameplay_assumption: A party first secretary, party president or constituent leader is not automatically a national president. The current single-office government engine does not model separate presidential and parliamentary mandates or cohabitation; a new named executive therefore requires an explicit presidential contender grant.

institutions.fact: The government must command the confidence of the House of Commons; party leadership and government formation are related but distinct.
institutions.gameplay_assumption: The exact pre-policy UK party terms retain their existing parliamentary gameplay selection behavior. This is a compatibility allowance, not proof of each person's Commons membership or eligibility on every reference date. New unreviewed terms are party-only.

institutions.fact: Constitution article 67 provides that the Diet designates the Prime Minister from its members. A party presidency is a separate office.
institutions.gameplay_assumption: The exact pre-policy Japan party terms retain their existing parliamentary gameplay selection behavior. This is a compatibility allowance, not a newly completed audit of every Diet membership interval. New unreviewed terms are party-only.

institutions.fact: The Bundestag elects the Federal Chancellor following nomination by the Federal President; the President appoints the elected candidate. Party chairmanship is a different office.
institutions.gameplay_assumption: New historical party offices are reference/party-only. Fictional party successors require a separately authored and reviewed executive contender grant before the existing government simulation can select their identity for national office. This gate does not add a full constitutional or nomination simulation.

institutions.fact: Constitution article 92 provides that the President of the Republic appoints the President of the Council of Ministers. The appointment is distinct from holding a party office.
institutions.gameplay_assumption: New historical party offices are reference/party-only. Fictional party successors require a separately authored and reviewed executive contender grant before the existing government simulation can select their identity for national office. This gate does not add a full constitutional or nomination simulation.

institutions.fact: The President appoints the Prime Minister under article 75(1); the official 2024 appointment explains the assessment of majority support in the Lok Sabha. Party chairmanship is not itself that appointment.
institutions.gameplay_assumption: New historical party offices are reference/party-only. Fictional party successors require a separately authored and reviewed executive contender grant before the existing government simulation can select their identity for national office. This gate does not add a full constitutional or nomination simulation.

institutions.fact: Constitution article 62 distinguishes National People's Congress selection of state offices, including the President and the Premier of the State Council, from political party offices.
institutions.gameplay_assumption: New historical party offices are reference/party-only. Fictional party successors require a separately authored and reviewed executive contender grant before the existing government simulation can select their identity for national office. This gate does not add a full constitutional or nomination simulation.

institutions.fact: The electoral court records the 1989 direct presidential election. Election to the federal presidency is a distinct process from holding a party administrative role.
institutions.gameplay_assumption: New historical party offices are party-only. A fictional successor needs an individually reviewed executive contender grant before a new named national-office selection. The government simulation still decides when succession happens; no national appointment is inferred from a party chair title.

institutions.fact: Under section 86 of the 1996 Constitution, the National Assembly elects the President from its members. This current institutional source is not projected backwards onto the different 1990 constitutional order.

The government simulation still decides when succession happens; no national appointment is inferred from a party chair title.

institutions.fact: The Governor General invites the person best placed to command House of Commons confidence to form a government. This is distinct from a party administrative appointment.

The government simulation still decides when succession happens; no national appointment is inferred from a party chair title.
